name: Ha Long Bay - Cat Ba Archipelago
place: Quang Ninh and Hai Phong, Vietnam
blurb: Limestone islands, reefs and mangroves, home to the rare Cat Ba langur.

tip.title: Cloud the water
tip.text: Plankton need light and clean water. Set Phytoplankton to -100% and watch zooplankton, oysters and anchovies fall, then the fish and porpoises above them.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Ha Long Bay - Cat Ba Archipelago

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Salt-tolerant trees of tidal flats around the islands. Wikipedia notes that tourism development has cleared mangroves in the bay.

nodes.name: Karst forest trees
nodes.desc: Leafy trees and shrubs that cling to the limestone slopes of the islands, forming the moist forest on which the langurs depend.
Small drifting animals, mostly copepods, that graze phytoplankton and are in turn eaten by corals, anchovies and larval fish.
The Cat Ba archipelago has about 178 coral species. Reefs in deeper waters are reported to be declining from pollution.
Warm tropical light drives the algae, seagrass and forest growth that start the web.
Cat Ba has no rivers, streams or permanent ponds, so the forest and langurs rely on rain collected on rock and plants.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Bacteria and fungi break down dead plants and animals on land and in the sea, returning nutrients.
